title:
Origins, Current
Practice, and Future Directions of
Life Cycle Assessment

affiliation.name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Life cycle assessment (LCA) has evolved from a niche method for evaluating product systems into a widely used approach for assessing the environmental sustainability of products, services, supply chains, technologies, sectors, economies, and scenarios. This article reflects on its historical roots, current state, and future developments. The early development was marked by pioneering methodological frameworks, inventory databases, and impact-assessment methods. Since then, LCA has matured into a robust and versatile method. Today, scientific, industry-related, and regional inventory databases support routine assessments, while impact assessment has increased in scope, accuracy, regional representation, and policy relevance. Advances in inventory modeling, impact assessment, regionalization, uncertainty analysis, and prospective assessment have substantially broadened the questions that LCA can address and the decision contexts it can support. While LCA traditionally focused on comparative assessments, recent advances introduced absolute approaches that benchmark impacts against planetary-boundary-based thresholds. Looking forward, artificial intelligence promises to transform LCA by facilitating data collection, enabling large-scale scenario analysis, and accelerating assessments. Moreover, increasing spatial and temporal resolution will be a game-changer for assessing impacts such as biodiversity loss and climate change.</jats:p>

title:
Endocrine-Disrupting
Effects and Reproductive Toxicity
of Metal-Based Nanoparticles through DRP1-Mediated Mitophagy within
an Adverse Outcome Pathway Framework
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The widespread use of metal-based nanoparticles (NPs), including Ag, ZnO, and TiO2 NPs, in industrial and consumer products has raised concerns about their potential endocrine-disrupting effects and reproductive toxicity. Conventional safety assessment approaches may not adequately capture the complex mechanisms underlying NP-induced toxicity. To our knowledge, this study is the first to integrate OECD-recommended assays, high-throughput screening, an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) framework, and the Toxicological Prioritization Index (ToxPi) to investigate the endocrine-disrupting effects and reproductive toxicity of metal-based NPs. The results showed that ZnO and Ag NPs increased estrogen receptor (ER) transcriptional activity, whereas TiO2 NPs inhibited it. All NPs increased 17β-estradiol production, while ZnO and TiO2 NPs reduced testosterone production. ZnO NPs induced the generation of reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial dysfunction, and DRP1 activation, which were associated with subsequent apoptosis, mitophagy, and autophagy. In contrast, Ag NPs did not induce apoptosis or autophagy, suggesting distinct cytotoxic mechanisms. TiO2 NPs caused no significant cell death in MLTC-1 cells, even at high concentrations. ToxPi ranked COOH-ZnO NPs as the most toxic, followed by NH2–ZnO NPs, Ag NPs, and TiO2 NPs. This integrated framework could provide a practical approach for toxicity screening, mechanistic investigation, and hazard prioritization of NPs.</jats:p>

title:
Temperature Does
Not Universally Accelerate VOC–OH
Reaction Kinetics: Implications for Ozone Formation

Spatiotemporal
Orchestration of Dual Functional Sites
Enables Efficacious NH3-SCR and CO Oxidation: Synergy
of Zeolite-Associated Cu Sites and Cu-O-Co Interfacial Ensembles

affiliation.name: Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Integrated abatement of NOx and CO is highly desirable for industrial flue-gas purification, yet competitive adsorption and mismatched kinetic requirements between NH3–SCR and CO oxidation hinder the realization of a unified low-temperature reaction window. Herein, a spatiotemporally organized Cu–O–Co/Cu-ZSM-5 architecture was constructed to provide differentiated catalytic environments and reduce mutual interference between the two reactions. The optimized Co0.2@Cu/Cu-Z5 catalyst delivers a broad co-operational window of 150–350 °C at 45,000 mL·h–1·g–1 and sustains simultaneous NO and CO conversions above 80% from 175 to 350 °C even at 175,000 mL·h–1·g–1, with high N2 selectivity and robust tolerance to 5 vol % H2O. In situ DRIFTS and transient cross-interference experiments indicate that zeolite-associated Cu species preferentially sustain NH3–SCR functionality, whereas Cu–O–Co interfacial ensembles preferentially enhance CO/NO oxidation, thereby alleviating mutual inhibition under coupled conditions. Theoretical calculations further reveal interfacial electron redistribution, Cu 3d-Co 3d hybridization, and more favorable oxygen-vacancy formation at the CuO/Co3O4 interface, and the CuO/Co3O4 interface lowers the activation barrier of the carbonate-forming elementary step from 2.12 to 0.36 eV via a carbonate-assisted MVK-like pathway, whereas its low activation barrier for the first NH3 dehydrogenation step (0.41 eV) suggests the necessity of confining NH3 activation to Cu-zeolite sites to avoid parasitic oxidation. This dual-center pathway differentiation alleviates adsorption and kinetic conflicts between competing reactions, offering a strategy for improving compatibility in multifunctional environmental catalysis.</jats:p>

title:
Temperature-Dependent
Decay of Infectivity of Infectious
Salmon Anemia Virus (ISAV) in Raw Seawater
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Infectious salmon anemia virus (ISAV) is an enveloped, single-stranded RNA, orthomyxovirus, distantly related to influenza viruses. ISAV poses a significant threat to global salmon aquaculture and wild fish and is a notifiable disease according to the World Organization for Animal Health. Understanding virus persistence in seawater under different environmental conditions is critical for biosecurity and disease mitigation. In this study, the persistence of ISAV infectivity was studied in raw seawater at five temperatures. Cell-culture propagated ISAV was incubated in raw seawater at 4, 7, 10, 13, and 17 °C for defined time periods. The persisting ISAV infectivity was then determined using an in vivo salmon fry challenge model, based on the assumption that the resulting infection prevalence correlates with the number of infectious ISAV virions present during the bath challenge. The results showed a clear temperature-dependence in infectivity persistence, with higher temperatures leading to faster decay of infectivity. The experimental data were used to estimate ISAV infectivity half-lives that were incorporated into a dispersal model to simulate the spread of infectious ISAV at different seawater temperatures. The modeling showed that the average potential exposure distance to infectious ISAV decreased approximately 40% when seawater temperature increased from 4 to 17 °C.</jats:p>

title:
Mapping Multiple
Pesticides in Vegetables from Major
Producing Areas across China: Coexposure Risk Assessment and Risk
Prioritization
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The application of various pesticides to ensure vegetable yields may result in the occurrence of pesticide residues as mixtures. However, information regarding the dietary exposure assessment and risk prioritization of multipesticides in vegetables remains limited. Here, we employed a suspect screening strategy to examine the occurrence of pesticides in 205 samples of cowpea, leek, and celery collected from markets and fields across 11 major producing provinces in China. Totally, 38 pesticides were identified, including 22 in cowpea, 25 in leek, and 23 in celery. Of these, the mean total concentrations of pesticides (∑Pesticides) were 163 ng/g, 96.3 ng/g, and 301 ng/g in cowpea, leek, and celery, respectively. Notably, fungicides and insecticides contributed to &gt;90% of ∑Pesticides, reflecting their extensive use in these vegetables. Exposure to pesticide mixtures was estimated to pose greater health risks than those of single exposure. Additionally, risk prioritization identified six high-priority pesticides (lufenuron, difenoconazole, λ-cyhalothrin, azoxystrobin, procymidone, and propiconazole; ToxPi score &gt;0.5) using the ToxPi framework. The predicted strong binding affinities (&lt;−7.0 kcal/mol) for 61.5% of the protein–pesticide complexes toward neurotoxic and endocrine-disrupting targets suggested potential molecular-level interactions linked to toxicological concerns of the identified pesticides. These results underscore the potential health concerns associated with coexposure to multiple pesticides in vegetables.</jats:p>

title:
Unresolved Complex
Mixture of Hydrocarbons as a Potential
Stratigraphic Anthropogenic Marker for the Great Acceleration

affiliation.name: Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research Warnemünde (IOW) , Seestrasse 15 , ,
Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research Warnemünde (IOW) , Seestrasse 15 , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The unresolved complex mixture (UCM) consists of chromatographically unresolvable branched, cyclic, and aromatic hydrocarbons, which are intermediate- to semivolatile organic compounds primarily derived from anthropogenic fossil fuel usage, including industrial emissions and gasoline and diesel exhaust. The UCM in natural archives, expressed as its ratio to resolved compounds (UCM/R), may thus provide an indication of fossil fuel-derived contamination in the environment over time. To test this hypothesis, accurately dated sediment records from the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea, and the northeastern Germany Tiefer See lake were analyzed for hydrocarbons. Each record presents a similar temporal pattern with a synchronous main increase of UCM/R in the early 1950s and a decrease in the 1990s. This UCM/R pattern most likely reflects the pronounced increase in the use of petroleum-derived products during the Great Acceleration of the mid-20th century and, subsequently, the application of filters and catalytic converters to reduce volatile organic compound emissions in the 1980s–1990s. Therefore, UCM/R in recent sediments represents a stratigraphic anthropogenic marker for the Great Acceleration in European midlatitudes and, if replicated globally, could be a further marker for the beginning of the Anthropocene as a potential geological epoch.</jats:p>

title:
Mapping Aluminum
Flows in the United States Using
Advanced Bayesian Material Flow Analysis
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system through 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework integrating system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. ARCADE combines government statistics, trade records, and industry reports into a physically consistent network and reports uncertainty-aware metrics. Results show continued U.S. reliance on imports of unwrought and finished aluminum products. The posterior median end-of-life (EOL) collection rate was 66.8% [57.2%, 79.9%] in 2017 and 67.6% [62.3%, 73.9%] in 2022. Median domestic retention of collected EOL scrap was lower in 2022 (52.7% [49.6%, 55.6%]) than in 2017 (56.4% [51.7%, 60.5%]), although the credible interval for the change spanned zero. Across robustness cases varying source weighting, pedigree-to-uncertainty mappings, and prior strength, domestic retention remained below 60%. Spatial analysis identified mismatches between EOL scrap generation and domestic remelting capacity. These findings show that improved collection alone may not increase domestic recycling when processing constraints persist. We observe a continued import dependence, efficient circulation of prompt fabrication scrap, and limited domestic retention of collected EOL scrap.</jats:p>

title:
Rapid
Emission–Economy Decoupling alongside
the Urbanization of Chinese Counties

affiliation.name: Sichuan Academy of Environmental Policy and Planning , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As China makes progress in air pollution control, the growing need for targeted pollution mitigation poses a great challenge for fine-scale emission tracking. However, the lack of up-to-date high-resolution emission data precludes a timely, spatially detailed assessment of emission distributions and their evolution with economic development. Here we derive summertime nitrogen oxides emissions from 2018 to 2024 for a total of 2,842 counties at different levels of urbanization in mainland China, based on satellite measurements and a fast, physics-based emission inversion method. The results show widespread declines in 84.1 ± 7.3% of counties. Among the 1,779 counties with available gross domestic product data, 76.7 ± 7.1% achieve absolute emission-economy decoupling (i.e., reduced emissions despite economic growth), and an additional 9.4 ± 3.9% exhibit relative decoupling (i.e., economic growth outpacing emissions growth). Relative emission reductions and emission-economy decoupling tend to be stronger in more urbanized counties, with the share of total national emissions moving toward less-urbanized, previously less-focused counties, particularly in the west. These results suggest structural progress toward greener development in Chinese counties along with an emerging need to shift attention toward less-urbanized locations.</jats:p>

title:
Ultrafast
NH4+ Capture by Prussian
Blue Analogues Accelerated by the Hydrogen-Bond of Water

affiliation.name: Shanghai Institute of Pollution Control and Ecological Security , ,

State Key Laboratory of Water Pollution Control and Green Resource Recycling , ,
Shanghai Institute of Pollution Control and Ecological Security , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Recovering ammonium (NH4+) from low-concentration wastewater represents a critical step toward sustainable nitrogen management. Although adsorption is widely regarded as the most promising strategy for NH4+ recovery from dilute streams, its practical application is often hampered by intrinsically slow kinetics and insufficient selectivity. Given the exceptional ion-sieving capability of Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), we hypothesized that water molecules confined within their framework channels create a dynamic hydrogen-bonded microenvironment that can modulate NH4+ transport. Inspired by this concept, we synthesized a series of Zn-based PBAs with controlled water contents via thermal treatment (denoted as Zn-PBAs-x, where x represents the treatment temperature). The sample with the highest water content (Zn-PBAs-60) exhibited an unprecedented NH4+ adsorption rate, with a pseudo-second-order rate constant (k2) of 4.35 g·mg–1·min–1. Integrated solid-state 1H magic-angle-spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (1H MAS NMR) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed a “water-accelerated adsorption” mechanism: hydrogen-bonding interactions between framework nitrogen sites and water molecules significantly weaken the binding of NH4+ to the framework, thereby markedly accelerating NH4+ migration within the channels. This material achieved nearly 20-fold concentration of dilute NH4Cl within 3 min. This study provides new insights and strategic directions for the rapid enrichment and resource utilization of low-concentration ammonia nitrogen, contributing to the advancement of sustainable development pathways.</jats:p>

Endocrine Diseases

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Phthalate esters (PAEs) are endocrine-disrupting chemicals that can imitate endogenous hormones to disrupt the endocrine system. However, the upstream molecular initiating events (MIEs) by which PAEs trigger endocrine diseases, especially their interactions with receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), remain poorly understood. Here, we discovered that the targets of low molecular weight (LMW) and high molecular weight (HMW) PAEs highly overlapped with breast cancer-related targets, with an even greater overlap for HMW PAEs. Mechanistically, PAEs promoted breast cancer progression by activating the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mediated signaling pathway, with EGFR identified as a key kinase. Molecular interaction analysis confirmed that PAEs directly bind to EGFR, inducing its dimerization, with the benzene ring, ketone, methyl, and ether groups of PAEs being crucial. Notably, HMW PAEs exhibited stronger dimerization effects. This PAE-induced EGFR dimerization was determined to be the MIE in PAE-induced breast cancer. Furthermore, PAEs increased EGFR expression (2.44-fold), subsequently activating the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, which promoted breast cancer cell proliferation to 165.34% and tumor growth to 229.05% of the control, with HMW PAEs again having stronger effects. This study identifies a previously unrecognized MIE–PAE-induced EGFR dimerization, linking PAE exposure to RTK–driven breast cancer and offering potential targets for prevention and intervention in breast cancer.</jats:p>

title:
Decoupling Ion Selectivity
and Transport via Dual-Scale
Interlayer Nanochannels in Reduced Graphene Oxide Membranes for Lithium
Separation
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Selective separation of Li+ from coexisting Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ is an important step in lithium recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) membranes offer a promising platform for this separation through their ångström-scale interlayer nanochannels. However, the same narrow nanochannels hinder ion diffusion, inducing a severe permeability–selectivity trade-off. To decouple ion selectivity from transport, we report a nanoconfined sol–gel strategy for constructing a dual-scale interlayer architecture in rGO membranes. Intercalated between graphene oxide layers, aluminosilicate (AS) sols serve as cross-linkers and in situ vapor sources. During thermal aging, sol–gel condensation generates vapor that expands un-cross-linked galleries into transport highways, while cross-linked domains retain ion-selective confinement. The architecture is tunable across ion-selective interlayer spacing (dS, 7.1–8.3 Å) and expanded interlayer spacing (dE, 34–94 Å). Compared with conventional rGO membranes, the optimized dual-scale spacing membrane increases Li+ permeability 5.4-fold in mixed-ion solution while achieving high divalent-ion selectivity (Li+/Ni2+ = 246, Li+/Co2+ = 391, Li+/Mn2+ = 448). Molecular dynamics simulations attribute this selectivity to asymmetric energy barriers imposed on Li+ and divalent cations within the cross-linked spacing, while the expanded spacing facilitates low-resistance transport. This work shows how nanoconfined sol–gel chemistry can open a design space for fabricating high-performance ion recovery membranes.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Antibiotics enter urban river basins mainly through sewage effluent. They undergo transformation during treatment and in river systems, generating transformation products (TPs) that may still have ecological effects. Yet, identifying these TPs by high-resolution mass spectrometry is hindered by the scarcity of reference standards and comprehensive MS/MS spectral libraries. To overcome this, we constructed a dedicated MS/MS library containing over 6,500 MS/MS spectra for 244 parent antibiotics and 362 TPs, thereby enabling rapid suspect screening through spectral matching. For novel TPs beyond library coverage, we integrated diagnostic fragment searching and seed-driven molecular networking to propagate annotations to structurally related unknowns. Applying this workflow to water, sediment, and effluent samples from an urban river system in Beijing, we identified 39 parent antibiotics and 158 TPs, of which 20 TPs are not previously documented in environmental samples. The major transformation reactions were cleavage, dealkylation, and hydrolysis, alongside compound-specific pathways like hemiacetal formation for erythromycin. These reactions differentially affect the environmental properties of antibiotics, and some reactions (e.g., dehydrogenation and dehydration) showed potential to enhance ecotoxicity. These results confirm that transformation substantially diversifies antibiotic signatures in urban aquatic environments and underscore the necessity of including TPs in environmental monitoring and risk assessment.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a crucial component of aquatic ecosystems, influencing pH, metal speciation, and the bioavailability of trace elements. The influence of DOM on water quality depends not only on its concentration but also on its chemical characteristics. To quantify the site density (SD) of organic acid functional groups, a key characteristic of DOM, this study utilized data from over 31,000 water samples collected from 110 watercourses between 1995 and 2024 by Swedish national monitoring programs. We found systematic dynamic trends in SD across Sweden. The analysis revealed an increase in SD from 1995 to 2003, followed by a decline from 2003 to 2010. Since 2010, SD has stabilized, although modest increases remain evident at many sites. Earlier trends were potentially governed by changes in DOM mobility associated with recovery from acid deposition, whereas more recent trends are likely linked to DOM source characteristics.</jats:p>

title:
Function of Submerged
Macrophytes in the Distribution
of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Alternatives in Constructed
Wetlands: Role of Extracellular Polymeric Substances (EPS) in the
Phyllosphere

affiliation.name: Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology, Chinese Academy of Sciences , , ,
China South-to-North Water Diversion Eastern Route Corporation Limited , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Submerged macrophytes in constructed wetlands (CWs) are key to removing PFAS alternatives, which pose serious risks to aquatic ecosystems. Although phyllosphere extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) are crucial for contaminant uptake by submerged macrophytes, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that typical PFAS alternatives, 6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate (F-53B) and hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), accumulated in Vallisneria spinulosa (V. spinulosa) reached 17.49 ± 1.02 and 5.25 ± 0.36 μg/g DW, respectively, approximately 2.70 and 3.16-fold higher than those in Ceratophyllum demersum (C. demersum). Correspondingly, the phyllosphere EPS of V. spinulosa exhibited high accumulation of GenX and F-53B, with concentrations of 124.98 ± 4.70 and 99.53 ± 13.12 μg/g DW, respectively. Crucially, EPS binding with PFAS alternatives increased the hydrophilicity and induced structural reorganization, facilitating contaminant internalization into plant tissues. Meanwhile, metagenomic analysis revealed that the phyllosphere microenvironment selectively enriched microbial functional genes involved in antioxidant defense and EPS biosynthesis, thus supporting sustained contaminant capture in the phyllosphere interface. These findings reveal EPS-mediated mechanisms underlying PFAS alternative uptake by submerged macrophytes in CWs.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Plankton constitutes the primary entry point of contaminants into pelagic food webs, yet the role of plankton size structure in governing hydrocarbon fate remains poorly understood due to methodological limitations. Here, polycyclic aromatic (PAHs) and aliphatic (AHs) hydrocarbons were investigated across seven plankton size fractions (0.7 μm to &gt;500 μm) collected in coastal waters of the northwestern Mediterranean Sea using a locally designed online sequential filtration system. Biochemical, isotopic, and molecular marker analyses were combined to characterize plankton composition, hydrocarbon sources, and PAH bioaccumulation patterns across size fractions. Molecular markers confirmed the transition from phytoplankton-dominated signatures in the smallest fractions to increasing zooplanktonic contributions in larger fractions. The 0.7–2.7 and 2.7–20 μm fractions, dominated by pico- and nanoplankton, accounted for the highest particulate organic carbon and hydrocarbon concentrations (3.0–3.4 μg g–1 dw for Σ26-PAHs) while zooplankton fractions (&gt;60 μm) displayed lower values (0.09–0.69 μg g–1 dw). The passive uptake of low-molecular-weight (LMW) PAHs dominated across all size fractions but decreased with increasing plankton size. In contrast, high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs showed preferential accumulation in nanoplankton. These results demonstrate that plankton size structure and biomass dependent processes strongly influence PAH bioaccumulation and trophic transfer in marine pelagic food webs.</jats:p>

title:
Microplastics
Promote
Light-Driven Ferrihydrite Transformation
by Altering the Balance between Interfacial Aggregation and Redox
Processes

affiliation.name: Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ferrihydrite (Fh) phototransformation regulates iron cycling and the mobility of nutrients and contaminants in aquatic and terrestrial environments. Microplastics (MPs) increasingly coexist with Fh, yet whether intact MP particles regulate Fh phototransformation through particle-scale interfacial effects remains unclear. We investigated how MPs (polystyrene (PS), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polylactic acid (PLA)) affect Fh transformation under simulated solar irradiation. Without MPs, irradiation produced predominantly hematite (Hm), with goethite (Gt) as a minor product, and 9.17% of Fh was transformed after 25 d. MPs increased the transformation without changing detectable products. MPs suppressed Fh reaggregation by shifting surface charge and disrupting Fh–Fh contacts, while enhancing irradiation-induced charge separation, surface Fe(III) reduction, Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling, and Fe mobilization. The promoting effects outweighed aggregation inhibition, causing net promotion of Fh transformation. Notably, PLA hydrolysis and photo-oxidation lowered pH and released acidic, Fe-complexing photoproducts, amplifying Fe mobilization and the aqueous Fe pathway. Overall, the PLA &gt; PVC &gt; PS trend reflects coupled polymer chemistry, particle properties, intact-particle interactions, and irradiation susceptibility, with PLA-derived aqueous components providing an additional solution-phase contribution. These findings show that intact MPs and polymer-derived aqueous products jointly modify Fe mineral evolution, linking plastic aging to iron biogeochemistry in illuminated surface environments.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Microbial decomposition in thawing permafrost mobilizes one of Earth’s largest organic carbon reservoirs, releasing CO2 that amplifies global warming. This carbon–climate feedback depends strongly on microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE)─the ratio of biomass carbon synthesis to total carbon uptake, which governs the balance between carbon retention and respiratory loss. Although permafrost carbon and microbial communities developed thousands of years ago, how paleoclimatic legacies shape permafrost CUE remains unresolved. Here, by integrating 18O–H2O labeling with amplicon and metagenomic sequencing across a ∼1000-km transect on the Tibetan Plateau, we show that mid-Holocene paleoclimate outperforms contemporary drivers in explaining spatial variation in permafrost CUE. Sites with drier and more variable paleoclimates exhibited lower CUE (0.17 ± 0.07) than wetter and more climatically stable sites (0.43 ± 0.08). This lower CUE was linked to two pathways: geochemical constraints involving reduced nutrient availability and stronger phosphorus limitation, and microbial adaptations reflected in communities enriched in metabolically costly stress-tolerance and recalcitrant carbon-acquisition traits. Collectively, these paleoclimatic legacies accounted for 70% of CUE variation, underscoring the critical role of paleoclimate in shaping the vulnerability of permafrost carbon to respiratory loss upon thawing. Incorporating these millennial-scale legacies into Earth system models could improve projections of future permafrost carbon feedbacks.</jats:p>

title:
A Substitution Paradox
in China’s Plastics
Sector: Climate Benefits of Degradable Materials Are Conditional on
Energy-System Decarbonization
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce reliance on fossil feedstocks and lower life cycle GHG emissions. However, their system-level climate effects remain uncertain because existing assessments often focus on individual products or polymers and rarely account for realistic substitution feasibility, value-chain interactions, and end-of-life (EoL) constraints. Here, we integrated dynamic material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, and scenario modeling to evaluate the net GHG implications of substituting degradable plastics across China’s plastics sector. The framework tracks five major conventional resins across 14 application sectors, links sector-specific substitution pathways with production-stage carbon intensities, and quantifies emission trajectories from 2025 to 2030, with long-term mitigation pathways explored to 2060. Technically feasible substitution increases cumulative life cycle GHG emissions by 7.1% relative to the conventional baseline because higher upstream production emissions outweigh potential EoL credits for recovered energy or displaced coproducts. Scenario analysis identifies a critical transition threshold: degradable plastics achieve net GHG reductions only when energy-system carbon intensity decreases by approximately 47% of the baseline level. The climate benefits of substitution are therefore conditional on coordinated energy-system decarbonization, production improvement, and waste-management development. Even under the optimistic pathway, 0.24 Gt CO2e of residual emissions remain in 2060, indicating the need for complementary mitigation measures.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Environmental DNA (eDNA)-based technologies have been increasingly employed in biodiversity surveys and ecological status assessments. However, most eDNA metabarcoding studies rely on relative read abundance, which limits their utility for quantitative environmental management and decision-making. To address this, we developed a quantitative calibration method incorporating dual internal standards: one added prior to DNA extraction and a three-concentration gradient added prior to PCR amplification, enabling independent correction of efficiencies for both steps. Results showed that within the tested aquatic matrices, DNA extraction efficiency had a greater impact on species quantification than PCR amplification efficiency. The dual internal standard calibration outperformed the single internal standard approach in both controlled laboratory experiments and field aquaculture ponds. The spiking of dual internal standards demonstrated excellent calibration across a wide range (2.4–54.1%), indicating that the method is broadly applicable and expandable without altering species detection. Field biomonitoring in the Yangtze River revealed that calibrated eDNA monitoring enhanced the spatial distribution patterns of an endangered species (Leiocassis longirostris) and a migratory species (Coilia nasus). Overall, calibrating DNA extraction and PCR amplification efficiency significantly improves the technical precision of eDNA quantification. While it strongly correlates with biomass under controlled conditions, in field applications, this dual calibration provides a robust analytical baseline that, when combined with ecological models, will be valuable for biodiversity conservation and ecological assessment. Pilot optimization of internal standard spiking volume is recommended for field surveys to balance sequencing cost and quantitative performance.</jats:p>

title:
Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure Promoted Vascular
Calcification through XBP1s-Associated Osteogenic Switching and Inflammatory
Crosstalk
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a major environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the mechanisms underlying long-term exposure-induced vascular calcification remain incompletely understood. Whether PM2.5 directly participates in mineral nucleation remains unclear. We found that PM2.5 accelerated the transformation of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) into crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) and may act as a heterogeneous nucleation interface under simulated physiological conditions. Mice were exposed to environmentally relevant PM2.5 concentrations (5 or 35 μg/m3) for 180 days using a whole-body inhalation system. Long-term PM2.5 exposure increased arterial stiffness and promoted vascular remodeling and calcification. Mechanistically, PM2.5 increased XBP1s expression in mouse aortic smooth muscle cells (MOVAS), promoting proliferative and osteogenic phenotypic switching. Genetic deletion of Xbp1 markedly attenuated PM2.5-induced MOVAS proliferation, migration, osteogenic transformation, and mineralization. In addition, PM2.5-stimulated MOVAS acquired a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype that promoted macrophage recruitment and M1 polarization, whereas Xbp1 deficiency attenuated these effects. We also established a human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid (BVO)-macrophage coculture system and found that macrophages substantially amplified PM2.5-induced osteogenic remodeling and calcification. Collectively, these findings revealed the involvement of both physicochemical mineralization and XBP1-associated osteogenic and inflammatory responses in PM2.5-induced vascular calcification, providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying PM2.5-associated vascular injury.</jats:p>

title:

Role
of Iron Redox and Microbial Adaptation
in Mediating Arsenic-Induced Suppression of Carbon Emissions in Paddy
Soils

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Arsenic (As) contamination disturbs organic carbon (OC) cycling in paddy soils, potentially influenced by microbial adaptive evolution and redox-active iron (Fe). Here, the association of As with C emissions (CH4 and CO2), microbes, and Fe dynamics in flooded paddy soils was investigated via microcosm experiments across two As levels (20 and 200 mg kg–1). Results showed that As contamination markedly inhibited CH4 (&gt;90%) and CO2 (&gt;38%) emissions, accompanied by inhibited ferric reduction, decreased OC bioavailability, and shifted microbial communities toward As-tolerant and oligotrophic strategies. Correlation analysis and validation experiments demonstrated that Fe reduction covaried negatively with available As but positively with C bioavailability indicators (p &lt; 0.001). The suppressed C emissions under low-dose As were closely linked to perturbed Fe redox cycling, while high-dose As appeared to amplify this inhibition through additional microbial toxicity and community restructuring. Exogenous zerovalent iron increased CH4 emissions by 0.92–19.54-fold through coupled changes in As immobilization, redox conditions, C bioavailability, and abundance of Fe-reducing bacteria and methanogens. This work indicated that Fe redox and microbial adaptation are important contributors to As-mediated suppression of C emissions, providing evidence for the As–Fe–C nexus and offering insights for balancing As remediation with C emission mitigation.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ion pairing, including contact, solvent-shared, and solvent-separated ion pairs (CIPs, SIPs, and SSIPs, respectively), affects aqueous reaction chemistry, sorption, and precipitation processes. Accurate characterization of ion pairing in aqueous sulfate electrolytes is essential for understanding their thermodynamics and hydration structure, yet comprehensive quantification across aqueous and mixed-solvent systems remains limited. We combine Raman spectroscopy with dielectric spectroscopy, using waveguide-based setups (WR-62 and WR-28, applied for the first time) and a broadband probe station (10 MHz–50 GHz), to characterize ion pairing and solvent–solute interactions in monovalent cation sulfate salts in water and water/methanol solutions. Dielectric spectroscopy resolved SSIP and SIP fractions, with SSIPs dominating Li2SO4 and Na2SO4. Raman spectroscopy quantified CIPs (K2SO4 &gt; Na2SO4 ≈ Li2SO4), consistent with cation hydration and polarizability. Methanol increased SIP and CIP concentrations. Ion association stability constants and mean activity coefficients were calculated with Archer’s form of the Pitzer model, incorporating short-range binary and ternary ion–ion interactions. This approach predicts mean activity coefficients at elevated ionic strengths without double-counting ion-pairing contributions, enabling determination of stability constants and aqueous speciation. Resolving ion-pair speciation is important for accurate thermodynamic models of sulfate-bearing waters relevant to membrane separations and resource recovery.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. Harmonized European surface water and groundwater monitoring data were combined with geostatistical interpolation and transport modeling to estimate contaminant concentrations at the groundwater table, while uncertainty in hydrogeological conditions, chemical fate, and preferential transport was propagated through Monte Carlo simulations. We compared a Surface Water Baseline scenario, based on model-derived groundwater concentrations and existing freshwater regulatory thresholds, with a Groundwater-Informed Conservative scenario integrating measured groundwater concentrations, groundwater-fauna toxicity data, and precautionary adjustments where groundwater-specific evidence was unavailable. Potential risk was summarized as the average frequency of exceedance (AFE) across contaminants and uncertainty realizations; its maps indicate the frequency and spatial distribution of threshold exceedances, not their magnitude or the severity of ecological damage. Mean AFE was low under the baseline scenario but increased 5-fold under the conservative scenario, revealing areas in the medium-to-very-high screening classes in the Pyrenean–Catalan sector, Sierra Nevada, and the eastern Balkan–Carpathian region. The framework provides a replicable basis for prioritizing monitoring, ecotoxicological testing, and management.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Acetonitrile (CH3CN) emitted from industrial production severely threatens atmospheric quality due to its persistence and high toxicity. While selective catalytic oxidation (SCO) represents the most promising technology for CH3CN elimination, the inherent competition between O2-activated oxidation and H2O-activated hydrolysis pathways has long prevented the simultaneous achievement of excellent low-temperature activity and high N2 selectivity. Herein, we report a Cu-modified TiO2 catalyst and propose a Cu-induced gradient-charge oxygen vacancy pair structure (Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti) as the most plausible active site configuration that enables activation of O2 and H2O via electron filling of their antibonding orbitals to promote the reaction during CH3CN oxidation. The electron-rich OVR site can adsorb both O2 and H2O, donating electrons to populate the π* antibonding orbital of O2 and the σ* antibonding orbital of H2O. Meanwhile, the electron-poor OVP site adsorbs O2 or H2O and serves as a reservoir to sustain a continuous supply of active species. The optimized catalyst induced by Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti structure achieves complete CH3CN conversion at 220 °C with 96% N2 selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of electron configuration in tailoring oxygen vacancy functions, providing a general strategy for developing advanced environmental catalysts for practical CH3CN emission control.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tire-derived p-phenylenediamines (PPDs) and their quinone derivatives (PPD-Qs) have emerged as potential neurotoxicants, yet the associations of prenatal exposure with offspring neurodevelopment remain underexplored. Therefore, we conducted a nested case-control study within a prospective birth cohort (n = 1,317) and measured ten urinary PPDs/PPD-Qs at 6–16 weeks of gestation. In the primary adjusted model, higher urinary concentrations of 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) and N,N′-di(o-tolyl)-p-phenylenediamine (DTPD) were associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay. Quantile g-computation further indicated that a simultaneous one-quartile increase in all components of the PPDs/PPD-Qs mixture was associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay (odds ratio = 1.33, 95% confidence interval: 1.03–1.72). Random forest analysis identified 6PPD-Q as having the highest variable importance among the measured PPDs/PPD-Qs. Network toxicology analysis implicated dopaminergic, serotonergic, and glutamatergic neurotransmission pathways as potentially relevant to 6PPD-Q-associated neurodevelopmental toxicity. In bEnd.3 mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells, 6PPD-Q exposure induced transcriptomic alterations involving xenobiotic metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and neurotransmission-related pathways. These changes were accompanied by decreased mRNA expression of the blood–brain barrier tight junction–related genes ZO-1 and occludin. Collectively, these epidemiological associations and complementary mechanistic findings support the biological plausibility of 6PPD-Q-associated developmental neurotoxicity and warrant further investigation and independent replication.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) in sedimentary formations requires understanding how hydrogen migrates, persists, and is released under nanoscale confinement in fine-grained rocks that may act as reservoirs or caprocks. Here, we combine in situ small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) with molecular dynamics simulations to examine how wetting state controls hydrogen reversibility and postcycling pore occupancy in shale nanopores. SANS-derived pore-size distributions reveal a clear hierarchy: dry shale exhibits near-complete reversibility, decane-saturated shale shows partial recovery, and water-saturated shale displays minimal recovery, with persistent postcycling occupancy concentrated in pores &lt;2 nm. Molecular simulations support a mechanistic interpretation in which this hierarchy arises from coupled nanoscale effects, including cavity-formation penalties, confinement-induced stress anisotropy, and fluid-specific interfacial free-energy barriers at mineral and organic surfaces. Water-saturated nanopores are associated with strong thermodynamic and mechanical constraints consistent with reduced hydrogen reversibility, whereas these constraints are substantially weaker in dry pores and intermediate in decane-filled pores. Together, the experimental and molecular simulation results provide a framework linking nanoscale fluid–rock interactions to hydrogen hysteresis and retention, with implications for subsurface hydrogen recoverability and containment in underground storage systems.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The 2022 Olympic Winter Games (OWG) and Paralympic Winter Games (PWG) marked the first time the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region implemented joint air pollution prevention and control measures for a winter mega-event. Notably, while Beijing maintained clean air (daily PM2.5 concentration ≤ 75 μg/m3, according to the Ambient Air Quality Standards in effect at the time) during the OWG, a heavy-pollution episode occurred during the PWG, with the 24-h average PM2.5 concentration peaking at 155 μg/m3. Combining field observations, dynamic emission characterization, and The Comprehensive Air quality Model with extensions (CAMx) simulations, we conducted a closed-loop study to investigate the underlying causes of this episode. Results show that while the industrial sector effectively regulated emissions, the mobile-source activity levels recovered rapidly after the Chinese New Year, outweighing the control measures implemented for mobile sources. This recovery increased total NOx emissions by 13% in the BTH region, driving nitrate-dominated PM2.5 pollution. During the study period, the PM2.5 nitrate concentration (normalized by the carbon monoxide concentration) was found to increase by 3 × 10–4 and 1 × 10–5 for each one-ton increase in NOx emissions in Beijing and the BTH region, respectively. To eliminate heavy PM2.5 pollution under the meteorological conditions observed during the PWG, NOx emissions would need to be further reduced by ≥1% in Beijing and ≥7% in the BTH region. This work underscores the urgent need to mitigate emissions from diesel trucks and nonroad machinery, especially under extremely adverse meteorological conditions in the BTH region.</jats:p>

title:

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada’s National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993–2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001–2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.</jats:p>

title:
Impacts of Biological
Filtration on Disinfection Byproduct
Control during Drinking Water Purification: A Critical Review
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, time-evolving ecosystems that can transition from a net “sink” to a net “source” of reactive precursors. This review synthesized evidence that biofiltration exhibits selective removal: hydrophobic and high-molecular-weight C-DBP precursors are preferentially removed, whereas hydrophilic N-DBP (e.g., HANs, NDMA) precursors readily break through and may be newly produced. The authors clarified the mechanistic basis of precursor generation, highlighting (i) biofilm turnover that releases intracellular organic matter enriched in amines and nucleic acids, (ii) continuous production and sloughing of soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances that elevate protein-like DON, and (iii) media aging and stratification that diminish removal efficacy. Regression analysis estimated sink–source transition for N-DBP precursor removal at approximately log10(bed volumes) = 5.38 (∼240,000 bed volumes), a practical reference in drinking water treatment plants. Furthermore, the authors identified critical operational tipping points, including oxidant pre-exposure, temperature fluctuations, and nutrient stoichiometry, that can trigger this functional inversion. Finally, a risk-oriented framework is proposed, advocating for precursor-specific monitoring (e.g., fluorescence signatures) and intelligent process control to stabilize biofilter performance against emerging genotoxic risks.</jats:p>

title:
Global Analysis
and Prediction of Bicarbonate in Groundwater
under Climate Change
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bicarbonate (HCO3–) is a major contributor to the alkalinity of groundwater, and low concentrations can reduce buffering capacity and increase the potential susceptibility of water to corrosion-related quality deterioration, particularly in untreated groundwater systems with corrosion-prone infrastructure. Here, we use machine learning and a comprehensive data set of 28,902 groundwater samples from 80 countries to produce a global probability map of HCO3– concentrations below 80 mg/L and estimate the population residing within the Low-Alkalinity Corrosion Risk Potential Zone (LACRPZ). From 2000 to 2020, LACRPZ was mainly concentrated in Southeast Asia and South America, with approximately 704 million people residing within these zones, particularly in Oceania (52.92%) and South America (35.09%). Although the area of LACRPZ is projected to decline under future climate change, the resident population in LACRPZ is expected to increase. This study reveals the evolution of global groundwater bicarbonate concentrations and resident population, underscoring the importance of integrating bicarbonate into water safety management strategies.</jats:p>

title:
Aldehyde-philic
Portal Engineering of γ-Cyclodextrin
MOF for Synergistic Capture of Toluene and Formaldehyde in Humid Atmospheric
Environments
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Efficient removal of multicomponent volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from real environments remains challenging, particularly under humidity. This study introduces an “aldehyde-philic portal modification” strategy that precisely anchors dopamine (DA) at γ-cyclodextrin-based metal–organic framework (γ-CD-MOF) outer rim via H-bonding to construct oligomeric polydopamine (o-PDA) structures. This pore design partitions the cyclodextrin cavity into an aldehyde-philic outer rim and arene-philic interior for efficient synergistic capture of formaldehyde and toluene in humidity. Exposed pyrrolic N sites on o-PDA enable γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 to preferentially bind CH2O, which then act as new sites to enhance subsequent C7H8 capture via CH−π interactions while hindering H2O binding to peripheral hydroxyls and preventing large-sized water clusters from blocking cavity openings. Furthermore, the hydrophobic inner cavity exhibits strong π–π conjugation with C7H8, facilitating its diffusion and establishing an “outer capture–inner fixation” pathway, significantly enhancing toluene capacity. At ∼40% relative humidity, the toluene working capacity of γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 in the multicomponent system increased by 106% over the single-component system, while the formaldehyde capacity remained unchanged. Consequently, the total working capacity of toluene and formaldehyde reached twice the sum of their single-component adsorption capacities, demonstrating marked synergistic coadsorption. This work provides a feasible approach for controlling multicomponent VOCs in complex humid atmospheric environments.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a key technology for carbon neutrality, but conventional CO2 geological sequestration suffers from high injection pressure, limited stability, and restricted storage space. Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration offers high capacity, low cost, and intrinsic safety. This study proposes a novel in situ CO2 hydrate formation and sequestration method in coal mine goafs containing permafrost layers in cold regions. The natural low-temperature permafrost environment provides favorable conditions for hydrate formation, while goafs offer large storage space. To avoid hydrate plugging and improve engineering feasibility, a liquid-first CO2 constant-pressure supply and predissolution mode was adopted. We simulated goaf conditions at depths of 110–130 m and ∼1 MPa. Experiments tested three injection temperatures (293.15, 298.15, and 303.15 K) and five goaf temperatures (269.15–277.15 K) using tetrahydrofuran and tryptophan as promoters. Results proved efficient sequestration at a low pressure of 1 MPa. Under optimal conditions (injection temperature of 298.15 K, goaf temperature of 271.15 K), capacity reached 60.9 mmol of CO2/mol of water (mmol/mol) with an efficiency of 135.36 (kg·m–3)/MPa. The 26.7 h stability experiments under depressurization showed 4.21–16.09 mmol/mol dissociated initially, but 66.38%–90.77% CO2 remained sequestered. Further, one-month tests under the pressure-release condition revealed hydrate dissociation almost stopped after day 1, yielding a 65.32% permanent sequestration ratio. Crucially, under the pressure-maintained condition, the system continued to form CO2 hydrates over the 30-day period, resulting in an additional 31.04% CO2 storage. These results validate the feasibility and long-term stability of this novel approach.</jats:p>

title:
Near-Real-Time
Mapping of Seamless All-Hour Aerosol
Optical Depth in China

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is central to assessing aerosol climate forcing and air quality, yet persistent cloud cover and the absence of nighttime satellite retrievals preclude seamless, all-hour monitoring. Here, we develop an automated machine-learning framework that fuses a newly available gridded visibility data set with forecast AOD and spatiotemporal covariates to reconstruct AOD over China at an hourly 5 km resolution in near-real-time. Trained on geostationary satellite observations, the model achieves robust performance (Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0.95 in cross-validation) and outperforms reanalysis and forecast products while filling cloud- and darkness-induced gaps. Independent validation against MODIS and ground-based nighttime Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) measurements yields consistent accuracy (MODIS R = 0.61 and AERONET R = 0.76), confirming physical generalizability. The resulting seamless record exposes a pronounced diurnal cycle with a midday minimum and an early morning maximum, and documents a consistent year-on-year decline from 2020 to 2022 that aligns with China’s clean-air actions and COVID-19 lockdowns. During a record-breaking dust storm, the framework tracks aerosol dynamics during cloud-obscured and nocturnal phases, capturing an uninterrupted process-level account of the event. By delivering the day–night aerosol continuum at high resolution and low latency, this work bridges a critical observational gap in air-quality response, data assimilation, and diurnal aerosol-climate research.</jats:p>

title:
TP-Agent: An Auditable
LLM Agent for Predicting Pollutant
Transformation Products in Oxidative Water Treatment
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Predicting the transformation products (TPs) of organic micropollutants is important for characterizing their chemical fate during oxidative water treatment and prioritizing candidate structures for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Limited labeled data and diverse reaction pathways make this task challenging. TP-Agent combines a large language model (LLM), training-only analog retrieval, and executable atom/bond edits to rank TP candidates with inspectable structural records. On 231 standardized-parent-disjoint reactions, TP-Agent achieved 78.8% strict Top-5 accuracy, compared with 65.8% for the bare LLM, 76.2% for standalone retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and 56.3 ± 1.5% for TP-Transformer across three training seeds. Parent-clustered bootstrap analysis supported the gain over the bare LLM; the 2.6-percentage-point difference from RAG was not statistically significant. Retrieval supplied most of the accuracy gain, while graph execution added candidate-linked structural records. Among 1095 candidates, 92.7% had exact edit-replay or deterministic-projection records, measuring structural linkage rather than mechanistic validity. Where available, candidate-linked LLM rationales provide chemical hypotheses for inspection. Estimated parallel latency and API-equivalent cost were 3.5 and 7.4 times those of RAG, respectively. TP-Agent thus combines TP candidate ranking with traceable structural operations and inspectable chemical hypotheses for HRMS follow-up.</jats:p>

title:
Solar-Driven Cu(II)–Cu(III)
Redox Cycle on
Decahedral BiVO4 for Scalable Water Purification
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Conventional Fenton-like reactions rely on external oxidants to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS, e.g., high-valent metal-oxo species (HVMS)), a practice that is inherently unsustainable for water purification. Here, we propose a solar-driven Cu(II)–Cu(III) redox cycle that differs from the traditional view that HVMS generation originates from peroxide-mediated pathways. By tuning the anisotropic built-in field of decahedral BiVO4, photogenerated holes accumulate selectively on its {110} family, enabling hole-driven hydrated Cu(II) oxidation instead of water. This facilitates an oxygen atom transfer (OAT) from adjacent Bi–OH sites to the H-bonded Cu(II) center, stabilizing the Cu(III)-oxo center by forming the Bi–O–Cu(III)–O structure (Cu(III)). Meanwhile, electron-driven dissolved oxygen reduction maintains charge balance. The photosynthetic Cu(III) mediates antibiotic degradation with a rate constant of 0.174 min–1, representing a ∼16-fold enhancement in the degradation rate constant compared to traditional photocatalysis. Crucially, the solar BiVO4 sheet/Cu(II) system sustains consistent up to ∼85% moxifloxacin degradation efficiency in each cycle over 35 days. No total Cu was detected in the effluent of cycling experiments after pH adjustment (∼7.5). These findings provide a new solution to the long-standing challenge of achieving peroxide-free HVMS synthesis and scalable water purification.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nonradical direct electron transfer (DET) can make advanced oxidation less vulnerable to radical scavenging in complex waters, but requires catalysts with efficient charge transport, stability, and practical synthesis. High-entropy materials provide diverse local environments, yet their multimetal compositions and prolonged heat treatment limit implementation. We combined chemically induced self-internal heating (SIH) with chloride-induced interfacial reconstruction to prepare a single-metal Cu system with high-density grain boundaries (SM-HDGB). SIH formed a Cu-carbon precursor in 3.5 s through an internal pulse above 1200 °C. HCl treatment generated intergrown Cu, Cu2O, CuCl, and Cu2Cl(OH)3 domains spaced 2–10 nm apart, creating phase, oxidation-state, and coordination diversity described as empirical interfacial chemical-state entropy. SM-HDGB completely removed tetracycline within 10 min and increased the apparent rate constant 9.88-fold over the precursor, with little response to 10 mM coexisting anions. Electron paramagnetic resonance, scavenging, filtration, electrochemical, and in situ spectroscopic evidence supported predominantly surface-confined, catalyst-mediated DET. In packed-bed operation, SM-HDGB maintained more than 80% COD removal across four regeneration cycles (approximately 130 h), retained pollutant-derived organic products, and produced near-neutral effluent compatible with Chlorella growth. Laboratory-scale screening estimated at least 96.3% lower synthesis energy demand than conventional routes. Chemical-state-diverse single-metal interfaces can therefore couple rapid peroxydisulfate activation with stable continuous-flow treatment.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Methylmercury (MeHg) compounds are classified as Group 2B agents, possibly carcinogenic to humans by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), and as Group C possible human carcinogens by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), but the carcinogenic implications of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure remain unclear. Here, we established a population-informed organoid-based strategy to explore the potential of low-dose MeHg exposure leading to cancer incidence. A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)-based analysis revealed nonlinear associations of blood MeHg with overall cancer history with increased predicted cancer probability around 5.39 μg/L for MeHg. Liver organoid experiments showed that low-dose MeHg did not cause overt short-term cytotoxicity but induced DNA damage and stress-response signatures after prolonged exposure. Transcriptomic analysis further linked low-dose MeHg exposure to cancer-related stress pathways, including reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated chemical carcinogenesis, p53 signaling, DNA repair, mitochondrial stress, and cell-cycle regulation. These results indicate that low-dose MeHg exposure could trigger early biological responses related to cancer-associated processes before apparent cytotoxicity occurs. This study supports organoid models as a human-relevant strategy for linking population exposure signals with tissue-level toxicological evidence in MeHg research and provides a potentially adaptable framework for evaluating subtle health effects of low-dose environmental pollutants.</jats:p>

title:
Investigating
the Relationships between the Structure
and Cytotoxicity of Ionic Liquids in the Context of Cell Lines Being
Affected
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Current quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models of ionic liquid (IL) cytotoxicity are generally developed for specific biological systems and cannot be assumed to transfer across cell types. Here, we evaluated 81 ILs spanning eight cationic head groups and 13 anions in HEK293T, CaCo-2, and DF-1 cell lines. The alkyl side chain length was the dominant structural determinant within homologous series, whereas cation, anion, and functionalization effects were most evident among ILs with shorter alkyl side chains. Mechanistic assays with 1-alkyl-3-methylimidazolium chlorides revealed distinct 24-h cellular response profiles in HEK293T and DF-1 cells, including different patterns of membrane permeabilization, apoptosis, and mitochondrial membrane potential changes. Descriptor-cytotoxicity correlations were strong within homologous imidazolium series but were less transferable across other structural comparisons. These results show that structure-based models can be informative within a defined chemical and cellular domain, but the cell type and cytotoxic response must be considered when extrapolating the IL cytotoxicity and assessing the safety of ILs proposed as greener process media.</jats:p>
